title: Elbow dislocation/instability – clinical and imaging analyses, reconstructions, and outcomes
summary:
Simple and complex elbow dislocations are being investigated to better understand injury patterns and the course of treatment. Patients are treated according to current guidelines, either conservatively or surgically, and are reassessed at 6 weeks and at 3, 6, 12, and 24 months. Clinical findings are recorded, imaging is used when necessary, and patients complete standardized questionnaires on pain, function, and satisfaction.

The aim of the study is to identify factors that can help guide the choice of optimal treatment and to improve long-term functional outcomes. The study will examine whether the frequency and type of elbow injuries are age-dependent. In addition, it will assess whether conservative treatment of stable, successfully reduced elbows with at most a minor ligament injury leads to satisfactory results. Finally, the study will analyze whether functional outcomes after surgery differ depending on whether primarily soft tissue or bone structures are affected.
